title: Synthesis of Decellularized Cartilage Extracellular Matrix Hydrogels
protocol: Take the collected cartilage and chop it into 1-2 mm³ pieces.
Place 20 g of minced cartilage in a 50 mL centrifuge tube, adding 20 mL of hypotonic Tris-HCl buffer.
Submerge the tissue completely with the buffer.
Freeze the tube at -80°C for 3 h and then heat it at 37°C for 3 h.
Repeat freezing and heating six times without replacing the buffer.
Shake the centrifuge tube using a vortex mixer at 1,000 rpm for 30 s.
Place a stainless-steel sieve on a new 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Decant the decellularized cartilage into the sieve, washing three times with sterile PBS.
Add 10 ml of trypsin solution (0.25% in PBS) and place the tube on a shaker at 37°C for 24 h.
Replace the trypsin every 4 hours during digestion.
Filter the suspension using the stainless-steel sieve, preserving the tissue.
Wash the trypsinized tissue with hypertonic buffer (1.5 M NaCl, 50 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.6).
Add 10 mL of nuclease solution to the tube.
Place the tube on a shaker at 37 °C for 4 h.
Remove the nuclease solution from the tube.
Wash the cartilage three times with sterile PBS.
Add hypotonic Tris-HCl solution to the cartilage.
Place the centrifuge tube on a shaker, and rinse for 20 h at room temperature (RT).
Remove the hypotonic Tris-HCl solution.
Wash the cartilage three times with sterile PBS.
Submerge the tissue in a 1% Triton X-100 solution for 24 h.
Remove the Triton X-100 solution from the tissue.
Thoroughly rinse the decellularized cartilage with distilled water for 3 days, changing the distilled water every 12 h.
Soak the cartilage in peracetic acid solution (0.1% PAA in 4% ethanol) for 4 h.
Remove the peracetic acid solution from the cartilage.
Wash the cartilage three times with sterile distilled water.
Place a stainless-steel sieve (pore size: ~250 µm) on a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Slowly decant the decellularized cartilage into the stainless-steel sieve to collect the cartilage.
Put the decellularized cartilage into a grinding bowl.
Add liquid nitrogen to the decellularized cartilage and grind it to form a powder.
Take 2 g of the decellularized cartilage powder.
Add 80 mL of 0.5 M acetic acid and 20 mg of pepsin to the powder.
Digest for 24 h at room temperature.
Centrifuge the mixture at 400 x g for 10 min.
Discard the sediment and collect the supernatant solution (DC-ECM solution).
Decant 1 mL of DC-ECM solution per well into 6-well plates.
Place the 6-well plates in a lyophilizer.
Freeze the DC-ECM solution until the temperature drops to −40 °C.
Turn on the vacuum pump once the temperature reaches −40 °C and maintain the vacuum degree at 10 Pa for 22 h.
Take out the freeze-dried DC-ECM solution from the lyophilizer.
Place the freeze-dried DC-ECM solution in centrifuge tubes.
Store the centrifuge tubes containing the freeze-dried DC-ECM solution at −20 °C.
Add 1 mL of sterile distilled water to dissolve 20 mg of freeze-dried DC-ECM solution in a centrifuge tube.
Shake for 1 min using a vortex mixer at a speed of 1,000 rpm at room temperature (RT).
Add 1 mg of vitamin B2 (0.1% w/v) to the DC-ECM solution.
Incubate the solution at 37 °C for 60 min.
Irradiate the solution with UV light (370 nm, 3.5 mW/cm²) for 3 min to form a hydrogel (DC-ECM hydrogel).
Take 20 mg of DC-ECM cartilage in a centrifuge tube.
Add 180 µL of Buffer GTL and 20 µL of Proteinase K to the tube.
Incubate the mixture at 56 °C for 4 h until the cartilage is completely dissolved.
Shake the centrifuge tube for 15 s using a vortex mixer at 1,000 rpm at room temperature (RT).
Add 200 µL of Buffer GL and anhydrous ethanol to the mixture.
Thoroughly mix by vortex vibration.
Centrifuge the samples for 1 min at a speed of 6,000 x g at 4 °C.
Add 500 µL of Buffer GW1 to the adsorption column.
Centrifuge the samples for 1 min at a speed of 12,000 x g at 4 °C.
Add 500 µL of Buffer GW2 to the adsorption column.
Centrifuge the samples at 20,000 x g at 4 °C for 1 min.
Add 50 µL of sterilized water to the adsorption column.
Centrifuge for 1 min at a speed of 6,000 x g at 4 °C to collect the DNA solution.
Determine the DNA content using a spectrophotometer.
Acidify 5 mg of decellularized cartilage with 5 mL of 6 M hydrochloric acid at 100 °C for 20 min.
Neutralize the mixture with 5 mL of a 6 M sodium hydroxide solution.
Measure the absorbance of the sample at 570 nm with a spectrophotometer to calculate the content of hydroxyproline.
Take 200 mg of DC-ECM cartilage powder and add 500 μL of Reagent A by vortex oscillation.
Incubate the sample at 4 °C for 16 h.
Centrifuge the sample at 14,000 x g for 10 min.
Take 50 mL of supernatant and add 50 μL of high-salt solution (Reagent B) by vortex oscillation.
Add 50 μL of acid solution (Reagent C) by vortex oscillation.
Incubate the sample for 10 min.
Add 750 µL of dye solution (Reagent D) by vortex oscillation.
Incubate the sample for 30 min in dark conditions.
Centrifuge the sample at 14,000 x g for 10 min and discard the supernatant.
Add 1 μL of cleaning solution (Reagent E) to the sample and mix well.
Centrifuge the sample at 14,000 x g for 10 min and discard the supernatant.
Add 1 μL of dissociation solution (Reagent F) to the sample and mix well.
Incubate the sample for 30 min under dark conditions.
Determine the GAG content using a spectrophotometer at 600 nm.
Place the decellularized cartilage sample in a 2.5% glutaraldehyde solution.
Incubate the sample at 4 °C overnight.
Wash the sample with PBS three times.
Fix the sample in 1% OsO4 for 1 h.
Wash the sample with PBS three times.
Dehydrate the sample by sequential immersion in 50%, 70%, 90%, and 100% ethanol, as well as 100% acetone for 15 minutes each.
Place the sample in a mixed solution of hexamethyldisilazane and ethanol (1:1) for 15 minutes.
Immerse the sample in pure hexamethyldisilazane for 15 minutes.
Place the sample in an HCP-2 dryer.
Dry the sample using liquid nitrogen.
Coat the fully dried specimen with a thin layer of gold-palladium using sputter coating at a power of 120 W for 5 minutes.
Image the coated sample using SEM under a working voltage of 15 kV and a vacuum degree lower than 5 x 10^-5 Pa.
Place the sample in a mixture of anhydrous acetone and resin (1:1) for 1 hour.
Place the sample in a mixture of anhydrous acetone and resin (1:3) for 3 hours.
Place the sample in resin overnight.
Embed the sample in embedding medium-filled capsules, and heat at 70 °C for 9 hours.
Cut the specimen into 70 nm thin slices using an ultrafine microtome.
Place the sliced specimen on a copper mesh.
Pipette 20 µL of uranyl acetate staining solution onto the copper mesh.
Stain the sample with uranyl acetate for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Gently wash the mesh twice with distilled water to remove the staining solution.
Pipette 20 µL of lead citrate staining solution onto the copper mesh.
Stain the sample with lead citrate for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Wash the mesh three times with distilled water.
Place the copper mesh onto a clean Petri dish lined with filter paper.
Air-dry the sections.
Photograph the sections using TEM.
